DI130* is a group of ICD-10 diagnosis codes used within the Danish healthcare system to identify cases of heart failure [^src1]. Specifically, it forms a critical component of the technical definition for heart failure within the Danish National Patient Registry (Landspatientregisteret) [^src1]. 

In the context of the AFDK (Atrial Fibrillation Database) 2025 report, DI130* is utilized alongside several other diagnostic codes (such as DI50*, DI110*, and DI420*) to define a hospital contact where heart failure is recorded as either a primary (A) or secondary (B) diagnosis [^src1]. This specific coding criteria is foundational for calculating [[hjertesvigtsindikatoren|Hjertesvigtsindikatoren]] (Indicator 15), which measures the occurrence of heart failure within one year following a new diagnosis of atrial fibrillation [^src1]. By relying on these specific ICD-10 codes from the national registry, the indicator tracks cardiovascular outcomes and quality of care, though it is subject to limitations such as the lack of coverage for general practice and underreporting tied to DRG-based registration systems [^src1].
